intro: Missouri runs its elections county by county, through a local election authority that is either a county clerk or a board of election commissioners.

id_rule.text: Bring one of these photo IDs: a Missouri driver or non-driver license, a military ID, a U.S. passport, or another photo ID issued by the U.S. or Missouri. It must not be expired, or it must have expired after the last general election. If you have none, you can vote a provisional ballot. It counts if you return with a photo ID the same day or your signature matches your registration record.

dates.label: In-person absentee voting, no excuse needed
dates.detail: From the second Tuesday before Election Day to the day before, you can vote in person at a place your local election authority picks. Show a photo ID.

src.label: Missouri Secretary of State, absentee voting

dates.label: Mail absentee ballot request deadline
dates.detail: Your local election authority must receive a mailed or faxed request by 5 pm on the second Wednesday before Election Day. To vote absentee by mail you must have one of the reasons in Missouri law, such as being away on Election Day or having an illness or disability.

src.label: Missouri Secretary of State, absentee voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6 am to 7 pm. Anyone in line at 7 pm has the right to vote. Bring a photo ID.
